name: Alaska
notes: The threshold comes from the Alaska Remote Seller Sales Tax Commission's code, which applies only to local jurisdictions that adopt it. Sales Tax Institute: the Commission passed its "Remote Seller Sales Tax Code & Common Definitions" that "would apply to local municipalities in Alaska that choose to adopt it"; registration is due "The first day of the month following 30 days from adoption by the city or borough". Commission page: "The remote seller's statewide gross sales, including the seller's marketplace facilitator's statewide gross sales, from the sale(s) of property, products or services delivered in the state meets or exceeds one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000)"; "Uniform Code as amended July 2024, effective January 1, 2025". effective_date is the date the current rule (no transaction threshold) took effect: Sales Tax Institute "Alaska removed their 200 transactions threshold effective, January 1, 2025"; Avalara lists the previous rule as "$100,000 or 200 transactions prior to January 1, 2025"; TaxJar "As of January 1, 2025, Alaska removed the transaction threshold". When individual municipalities adopt the code varies: "Varies by district" (Avalara), "Various adoption dates by municipalities" (Sales Tax Institute); TaxJar lists "January 6, 2020" (with a 30-day local adoption period) as the original effective date.

notes: Both thresholds must be met ("and"). Comparator is not recorded: "more than" is stated for the 100-sale count, but no cited page states the wording of the current $500,000 dollar threshold.
